content.section_title: 8.4 Treatment of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
content.summary: To date no treatment has convincingly reduced mortality and morbidity in HFpEF overall; some trials showed improvements for specific phenotypes but large RCTs failed primary endpoints.
trial_findings: Hospitalizations for HF were reduced by candesartan and spironolactone; trend towards reduction with sacubitril/valsartan though trials were neutral for primary endpoints.
Nebivolol reduced a combined endpoint in SENIORS but that trial included only 15% with LVEF >50%.
content.other_trials_and_outcomes: Trials targeting the nitric oxide–cGMP pathway and several phenotype-specific trials (NEAT-HFpEF, INDIE-HFpEF, VITALITY-HFpEF, CAPACITY-HFpEF) failed to improve exercise capacity or quality of life.
content.treatment_practice_at_baseline: In PARAGON-HF at baseline >86% of patients were on ACE-I/ARBs, 80% on beta-blockers, and >24% on MRAs.
content.clinical_note: Despite lack of disease-modifying therapies, many HFpEF patients are treated for comorbid hypertension and CAD with ACE inhibitors/ARBs, beta-blockers, or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.

Associated Conditions: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
genes.context: Text notes many patients are treated with ACE-I/ARBs; in PARAGON-HF >86% of patients were on ACE-I/ARBs at baseline.
